analysis.investment_thesis: Unisem Agritech is a tiny (INR 68 Cr) seed company earning a paltry 0.57% ROE — well below a savings account — yet trading at 15.9x earnings, which is absurd for such wretched returns on capital. This is a fair business at an unfair price, and well outside any margin of safety.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 70.88% signals owner alignment
Agri-inputs sector benefits from structural Indian demand
key_risks: ROE of 0.57% is catastrophically below cost of capital
P/E of 15.9x on near-zero earnings implies extreme overvaluation on normalized basis
Nano-cap (INR 68 Cr) seed business with no demonstrable moat vs. entrenched players (Kaveri, Mahyco, UPL)
red_flags: ROE under 1% — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
Young company (founded 2016) with unproven earnings durability
Commodity-like seed business with weather, regulatory, and monsoon cyclicality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
A business that earns 0.57% on shareholders' equity is not a business I would own at any price, let alone 15.9x earnings. Charlie and I have always said that over the long run, your returns as an owner approximate the ROE of the underlying business — at 0.57%, you would be better off in a post office deposit. The seed industry in India can be attractive (Kaveri Seeds has historically earned 20%+ ROE) but Unisem is clearly sub-scale and has no pricing power, no distribution moat, and no demonstrated capital allocation track record since its 2016 incorporation.

The 70.88% promoter stake is the one redeeming feature, but promoter alignment without competent capital allocation is merely a passenger sitting next to a bad driver. At INR 68 Cr market cap with these returns, this is a speculation, not an investment. I'll pass and wait for the pitch down the middle.
